mse.def: \(\frac1n\sum_i (y_i-\hat f(x_i))^2\): the average squared prediction error.

training-mse.def: The MSE computed on the same observations used to fit the model; it always falls as flexibility rises.

test-data.def: Observations not used to train the method, used to measure how well it predicts new data.

test-mse.def: \(\text{Ave}(y_0-\hat f(x_0))^2\) over previously unseen test observations; usually U-shaped in flexibility.

flexibility.def: How wide a range of shapes a method can fit; measured e.g. by degrees of freedom.

degrees-of-freedom.def: A number summarising a fit's flexibility, roughly how many parameters it is free to choose (2 for a straight line).

overfit2.def: Small training MSE but large test MSE, where a less flexible model would have given a smaller test MSE.

variance-method.def: How much \(\hat f\) would change if estimated from a different training set; increases with flexibility.

bias.def: Error from approximating a complicated real problem by a simpler model: \(\E\hat f(x_0)-f(x_0)\); decreases with flexibility.

bv-tradeoff.def: Expected test MSE = variance + bias² + Var(ε); lowering one of the first two usually raises the other, so test error is minimised at intermediate flexibility.

error-rate.def: The fraction of observations misclassified, \(\frac1n\sum_i I(y_i\ne\hat y_i)\).

indicator.def: \(I(\text{statement})\): 1 if the statement is true, 0 if false.

conditional-probability.def: \(\Pr(Y=j\mid X=x_0)\): the probability that \(Y=j\) given that \(X=x_0\).

bayes-classifier.def: Assigns each observation to the class with the largest \(\Pr(Y=j\mid X=x_0)\); has the lowest possible test error rate.

bayes-boundary.def: The set of points where the two most likely classes are equally probable (50% for two classes).

bayes-error.def: \(1-\E(\max_j\Pr(Y=j\mid X))\): the lowest achievable test error rate; the classification analogue of irreducible error.

knn.def: Classify \(x_0\) by a majority vote of the \(K\) training points closest to it; class probabilities are the fractions of neighbours in each class.
